daily_brief: The day's most significant developments center on the ongoing US-Iran conflict, European wildfires, and a deadly attack in Berlin. After nearly two weeks of nightly US bombardments on Iran, operations have paused, with reports suggesting dwindling munitions stockpiles may be constraining Washington's options [France 24, ABC Australia, The Hindu]. Diplomatic efforts continue, with an Omani delegation in Tehran for talks on the Strait of Hormuz. In Europe, devastating wildfires have displaced over 330,000 people across France and Spain, with France mobilizing military assets including an A400M cargo plane to combat blazes threatening Bordeaux [BBC, RFI, Globe and Mail]. The Tour de France's final stage was shortened to redeploy security personnel. In Berlin, a van attack on Pride celebrations killed one person and injured at least 16 others; police have identified a 21-year-old suspect with alleged ties to Islamist groups and warned he may be armed [France 24, Le Monde, Financial Times]. Meanwhile, Russian ballistic missile strikes on a drone exhibition near Kyiv killed at least 10 people and injured around 100 [BBC], and India's Education Minister resigned following weeks of youth-led protests over examination irregularities [BBC].

top_stories.headline: US Pauses Iran Strikes Amid Reports of Dwindling Munitions Stockpiles
bullets: The US military conducted no strikes on Iran overnight Saturday-Sunday, ending nearly two weeks of consecutive nightly bombardments
US media reports cite concerns over depleting Patriot interceptor and air defense munitions stockpiles as a factor in the operational pause
An Omani delegation arrived in Tehran for talks on Strait of Hormuz management; the US naval blockade remains in effect
Iran's Houthi allies claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia's Jizan province in retaliation for Saudi strikes on Hodeida

top_stories.headline: Wildfires Displace Over 330,000 Across France and Spain; Tour de France Shortened
bullets: More than 330,000 people have been evacuated across France and Spain, with 220,000 displaced in France alone
France deployed military assets including an A400M cargo plane to drop flame retardant; 42,000 hectares have burned near Bordeaux
One person died in Manises, Spain, marking the first fatality from the blazes
The Tour de France final stage was reduced by one-third to allow security personnel redeployment to fire zones

top_stories.headline: Van Attack at Berlin Pride Kills One, Injures 16; Suspect With Islamist Ties Sought
bullets: A white van drove into crowds at Berlin's LGBTQ+ Pride celebration Saturday night, killing one and injuring at least 16, some critically
German authorities issued a wanted notice for a 21-year-old suspect identified as Abdul B., warning he may be armed and dangerous
Berlin police confirmed the suspect has known ties to Islamist groups in the city
Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the incident 'an attack on our society'; the event and concert were cancelled

top_stories.headline: Russian Missile Strikes Kill 10 at Ukraine Drone Exhibition Near Kyiv
bullets: Russian ballistic missile strikes hit a drone technology exhibition near Kyiv, killing at least 10 people and injuring approximately 100
The daytime attack targeted an event attended by prominent defense sector figures; key officials later confirmed they were unharmed
Five additional people were killed by Russian glide bombs in Sloviansk; two died in Sumy
President Zelensky warned of intelligence indicating Russia was preparing another massive missile strike within 48 hours

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Detailed coverage including Ukrainian counterstrike on Russian city of Kirov

top_stories.headline: India's Education Minister Resigns After Weeks of Youth-Led 'Cockroach' Protests
bullets: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following five weeks of protests organized by the satirical 'Cockroach Janta Party' movement
The AI-generated cockroach mascot became a symbol for youth frustration with examination irregularities and government policies
Protests intensified after Monday's police crackdown on marchers heading to parliament left dozens injured
The CJP called off demonstrations following the resignation, declaring a victory for democracy

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the novel nature of the AI-mascot protest movement and its evolution into a serious political force
